report.source_text: To investigate the hypoxia a chest and abdomen computed tomography (CT) with administration of intravenous contrast material was ordered. The exam showed a group of dilated vessels in right upper and lower pulmonary lobes. These lesions were reported as likely arteriovenous malformations (PAVM) (Figure 1 and 2). The CT of the abdomen was unremarkable.

report.source_text: Gastroduodenoscopy and colonoscopy were normal, while a capsule endoscopy documented multiple telangiectasias in the jejunum, and oral iron supplements were started after a blood trasfusion.

clinician.final_diagnosis: The association of recurrent nasal bleeds, cutaneous telangiectasias and visceral vascular malformations allowed us to diagnose HHT (see below).
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old woman presented with seizures, transient left hemiparesis, severe hypoxemia, epistaxis, exertional dyspnea, and cutaneous telangiectasias. Workup revealed an ischemic stroke in the cerebellum, pulmonary arteriovenous malformations (PAVMs) in the right lung, and multiple telangiectasias in the jejunum. These findings, including recurrent nasal bleeds, cutaneous telangiectasias, and visceral vascular malformations (PAVMs and jejunal telangiectasias), supported the diagnosis of Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT). She received a blood transfusion and oral iron supplements.
